title: Move boxes between three levels
summary: Make two lifts work at the same time, each in its own cycle, meeting only at the belt between them.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Describe each lift as a cycle of steps of its own that returns to where it began.
Make both lifts work at the same time, meeting only at the belt between them.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ThreeLevelLifts.sfc.json, lift A already carries each box from the infeed to the transfer belt at level 2. Lift B must carry each box from the transfer belt up to the outfeed at level 3, as lift A does one level lower, and both lifts must be able to work at the same time.
stages.checkpoint: Reading the active steps tells you what each lift is doing at any moment.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow one box: it rides the infeed onto lift A, A rises with its surface stopped, runs the box onto the transfer belt at level 2 and lowers; B does the same one level higher and hands the box to the outfeed.
stages.checkpoint: Each lift's belt is stopped while the lift moves, the transfer belt stops when EyeMid sees a box, and Green lights when the fifth box, released 50 s into the run, reaches EyeTop.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Make lift B carry the boxes on from the transfer belt to level 3 while lift A keeps working, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program runs only lift A, so the boxes pile up on the transfer belt and none reaches the bin.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named three-level-lifts and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch both lifts in the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}: at times they move at the same time, and the transfer belt at level 2 is the only part that both of them use.
stages.checkpoint: Both lifts are seen moving at the same time for a while, boxes reach the outfeed one after another, and no box is dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The EVENTUALLY assertion proves a box reached the top bin, the AT assertion proves Green is lit at the end and the ALWAYS assertion proves no box fell.
stages.checkpoint: The grade cannot see the order of the steps of each lift, nor whether a lift moved while its surface ran; it sees only what arrived and what fell.

hints.text: Lift B does the same job as lift A, one level higher. Look at how the cycle of lift A is built, then ask which signals and outputs of lift B play the same part, and what has to be true for both lifts to be working at the same time.

Copy the five steps of lift A and rename them B_LOAD to B_LOWER; lift B reads BAtLow, BAtHigh and BoxOnB, and sets BLoading instead of RunInfeed. Copy their actions and transitions; B writes BRun, BUp and BDown where A writes ARun, AUp and ADown; B_LOWER returns to B_LOAD, and B's actions leave out A's AUnloading assignments. Then start both chains with one transition: give the start transition a second target in toSteps, which is B_LOAD, and keep the two chains apart from then on.

faultCases: The starting program runs only lift A, so the boxes pile up on the transfer belt and none reaches the bin.
